mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5.25% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 exceeding 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives lower equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered quarters, or the average return is not significantly below the median baseline at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and cost margins, ultimately compressing profit growth and leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent acceleration in INDPRO (above 0.5% monthly) and a deceleration in HOUST (below 1.5% monthly) for two months signals a divergence between industrial production and housing demand, indicating a risk of demand-supply imbalance that reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0.5% and HOUST < 1.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the median return is not statistically below the baseline at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month drop in FEDFUNDS below 3.0% during a period of negative GDP growth signals an emergency easing, which boosts liquidity and risk appetite, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops > 1.0pp in one month AND GDPC1 YoY < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically above zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sequential rise in RSAFS and PAYEMS over three consecutive months signals strengthening household balance sheets and rising consumption, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and PAYEMS both rising for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically above the baseline at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in UNRATE below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals a loosening labor market, which reduces wage inflation and cost pressures, supporting profit margins and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically above zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in INDPRO above 0.3% for six consecutive months signals robust industrial production growth, which raises earnings expectations and supports higher equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the median return is not statistically above the baseline at 95% confidence.
